subject: maths
title: Chapter 6 · Test 3
summary: Chapter 6 test 3: index laws, zero and negative indices, scientific notation, introducing surds and simplifying surds.
body:
This test covers all of Chapter 6, Indices and surds: the index laws, zero and negative indices, scientific notation, what surds are and how to estimate them, and simplifying, adding and multiplying surds.

There are 15 questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes, no notes, no calculator unless the question says. Write your working on paper. Give exact answers as surds in simplest form, and check that scientific notation answers have one non-zero digit before the decimal point. When you finish, check any you got wrong using the steps and the notes on each wrong answer.

questions.explanation: (p⁴)⁶ means multiply the indices: 4 × 6 = 24, so p²⁴. p¹⁰ adds them instead.
steps: (p⁴)⁶ is a power of a power, so multiply the indices.

mistakes.A: Step 1: a power of a power means multiply the indices, not add them.
mistakes.B: Step 1: the 6 is an index on the bracket, not a coefficient.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the 24 is the new index — it stays raised on the p.

questions.explanation: 10⁻³ = 1/10³ = 1/1000 = 0.001. −1000 treats the negative index as a minus sign.

mistakes.B: Step 1: a negative index means the reciprocal, not a negative number.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 1/1000 has 3 decimal places — you used 4.
mistakes.D: Step 1: don't multiply the base by the index. 10⁻³ means 1 ÷ 10³.

questions.explanation: Move the point 4 places right: 1.08 → 10.8 → 108 → 1080 → 10 800. 1080 moves only 3 places.
steps: The index is +4, so move the point 4 places right.

mistakes.A: Step 2: move the point 4 places, not add 4 zeros after 108.
mistakes.B: Step 2: move the point 4 places right — you moved it 3.
mistakes.D: Step 1: a positive index moves the point right, making the number bigger.

questions.explanation: √18 = √9 × √2 = 3√2. 9√2 takes 9 out without square rooting it.
steps: The largest perfect square factor of 18 is 9 (18 = 9 × 2).

mistakes.A: Step 1: 18 = 9 × 2, so 9 is the perfect square. You swapped the numbers.
mistakes.C: Step 2: only the square root of 9 comes out: √9 = 3.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 18 = 6 × 3 doesn't help — 6 is not a perfect square.

questions.explanation: 9 = 3², so 9⁴ = (3²)⁴ = 3⁸. Check: 9⁴ = 6561 = 3⁸ ✓. 3⁶ adds the indices instead of multiplying.

mistakes.A: Step 2: (3²)⁴ is a power of a power — multiply 2 × 4, don't add 2 + 4.
mistakes.C: Step 1: changing the base from 9 to 3 changes the index too: 9 = 3², not 3.

questions.explanation: 10⁰ = 1 and 10⁻¹ = 0.1, so the total is 1.1. 0.1 treats 10⁰ as 0.
From 3.9 to 3 900 000 000 the point moves 9 places right, so 3.9 × 10⁹. 3.9 × 10⁸ counts the zeros instead.
steps: Put the point after the first digit: 3.9.
Count the moves back to 3 900 000 000: 9 places right, so 3.9 × 10⁹.

mistakes.B: Step 2: count the places the point moves (9), not the zeros (8).
mistakes.C: Step 1: the first number must be at least 1 and less than 10.
mistakes.D: Step 2: count the moves carefully — from 3.9 the point moves 9 places, not 10.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a surd?
questions.explanation: √0.25 = 0.5 because 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25, so it is rational, not a surd. √12, √15 and √50 are all irrational.
steps: A surd is a root that is irrational.
0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25, so √0.25 = 0.5, a rational number. It is not a surd.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 12 is not a perfect square, so √12 ≈ 3.464… never ends or repeats. It is a surd.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 15 is not a perfect square, so √15 is irrational — a surd.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 50 is not a perfect square (it is between 49 and 64), so √50 is a surd.

questions.explanation: √60 ÷ √5 = √(60 ÷ 5) = √12 (which can also be written 2√3). 12 drops the root sign.

mistakes.B: Step 1: the rule divides under the root (60 ÷ 5), it doesn't subtract.
mistakes.C: Step 1: √60 ÷ √5 = √12 — the root sign stays, because 12 is not a perfect square.
mistakes.D: Step 1: this is a division — you multiplied 60 × 5.

questions.prompt: Calculate (5 × 10³)². Give your answer in scientific notation.

mistakes.A: Step 3: when 25 becomes 2.5, add 1 to the index.
mistakes.D: Step 2: (10³)² = 10³ˣ² = 10⁶. Multiply the index by 2; don't square it.

questions.prompt: Find the exact length of x in this right-angled triangle, in simplest surd form.
questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with both shorter sides 6 cm; the hypotenuse is labelled x.
questions.explanation: x² = 6² + 6² = 72, so x = √72 = √36 × √2 = 6√2 cm. 36√2 takes 36 out without square rooting it.

mistakes.A: Step 1: Pythagoras squares the sides first: 6² + 6², not 6 + 6.
mistakes.B: Step 2: √72 = √36 × √2, and √36 = 6 — take the root of 36.
mistakes.C: Step 1: square each side before adding: 36 + 36 = 72, not 6 + 6 = 12.

questions.prompt: Simplify (x⁻²)³ × x⁹, using positive indices only.
questions.explanation: (x⁻²)³ = x⁻⁶, then x⁻⁶ × x⁹ = x³. x¹⁰ adds −2 and 3 in the bracket instead of multiplying.

mistakes.A: Step 1: (x⁻²)³ is a power of a power — multiply −2 × 3, don't add −2 + 3.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you are multiplying by x⁹, so add the indices (−6 + 9), don't subtract.
mistakes.D: Step 2: −6 + 9 = +3, so the index is positive — nothing moves under the line.

questions.explanation: The top is 12x⁶y⁴, and 12x⁶y⁴ ÷ 4x³y² = 3x³y². 3x²y² divides 6 by 3 instead of subtracting.
steps: Top first: 6 × 2 = 12, x⁴ × x² = x⁶, y³ × y = y⁴, giving 12x⁶y⁴.
Divide by 4x³y²: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, x⁶⁻³ = x³ and y⁴⁻² = y², so 3x³y².

mistakes.B: Step 2: divide the coefficients (12 ÷ 4), don't subtract them.
mistakes.C: Step 2: dividing powers means subtract the indices, not add them.
mistakes.D: Step 2: x⁶ ÷ x³ = x⁶⁻³ = x³ — subtract the indices, don't divide them.

questions.explanation: 3√8 = 6√2 and √18 = 3√2, so 6√2 − 3√2 + √2 = 4√2. Getting 0 forgets the 3 in front of √8.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the + √2 is added, not subtracted: 6 − 3 + 1.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 3√8 = 3 × 2√2 = 6√2 — don't forget to multiply by the 3.

questions.prompt: In a model, one dust particle has a mass of 3.2 × 10⁻⁹ kg. What is the total mass of 5 × 10⁶ of these particles? Give your answer in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: (3.2 × 10⁻⁹) × (5 × 10⁶) = 16 × 10⁻³ = 1.6 × 10⁻² kg. 1.6 × 10⁻³ forgets to adjust the index.

mistakes.A: Step 3: when 16 becomes 1.6, the index goes up by 1: −3 + 1 = −2.
mistakes.C: Step 1: total mass = mass of one × number of particles, so multiply — don't divide.
mistakes.D: Step 2: multiplying powers of 10 means add the indices (−9 + 6), not multiply them.
